title: moon upgrade deletes lib and include before the replacement exists, so any later failure leaves the toolchain unusable

labels.name: pending-triage
labels.description: This issue is not confirmed yet, and/or hasn't been checked for priority

body:
## Actual behavior

`moon upgrade` hands off to a remote installer (`powershell.ps1` / `unix.sh`) that
deletes the old toolchain before it has a new one. Both installers are
destroy-then-rebuild:

```
powershell.ps1   download moonbit.zip → Remove-Item lib, include → Expand-Archive
                 → Remove-Item lib\core → download core.zip → moon bundle
unix.sh          download tarball → rm -rf lib include → tar xf
                 → rm -rf lib/core → download core → bundle
```

Extraction, the core download, or the bundling can fail; Ctrl-C during the (slow)
bundling; a running `moon-lsp.exe` can lock a binary mid-extract (#1878). All of
these happen after the only copy of `lib`/`include` is gone, and nothing restores
it. `moon check` then fails everywhere with:

    Cannot inject the standard library `moonbitlang/core`: Cannot load the core file

The only rollback moon has is `copy_moon_back()`, which restores `moon.exe` and
nothing else. moon also self-deletes the running executable before the script
starts and restores it only on the non-zero-exit and Ctrl-C paths — a closed
console loses both `moon.exe` and `lib`.

There is a quieter variant: the generated `script.ps1` has no
`$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"`, so a failed `irm` (plain network hiccup) is a
non-terminating error and powershell still exits 0. moon reports "Done" while
`moon.exe` is already gone.

What is lost: `lib` is ~450 MB, almost all of it the bundled core plus the
native-link artifacts shipped by `moonbit-*.zip` (`libmoonbitrun.o`, `libtcc1.a`,
`runmain.o`, …). Re-downloading `core-latest.zip` — the usual recovery — restores
`lib/core` only, so native linking stays broken.

This is not #2594. That fixed one trigger (a leaked `PSModulePath` breaking
`Expand-Archive`); the delete-before-extract ordering and the missing rollback are
unchanged, and any other interruption reproduces the same end state.

This also outlives the planned removal of the bundle process (#2380/#2381): whatever
replaces the bundled core still has to be downloaded and swapped in by the same
installers, so the delete-first ordering and the missing rollback remain.

Side note, same class of "commit before verify": the moonbit and core downloads
both carry the literal `latest`, resolved server-side at two different moments, so
a release landing in between installs a `moonc` and a `core` from different
versions.

## Expected Behavior

Build the replacement before touching `$MOON_HOME`: download both archives, extract
into a staging directory on the same volume, run `bundle` against the staging tree,
verify (`lib/core` with its manifest, `include`, `bin/moonc`), then swap and delete
the old tree. Simply removing the delete is not a fix — `Expand-Archive -Force`
overwrites but never prunes, so stale files from the previous version would
survive.

A moon-side stopgap is in preparation (PR to follow): snapshot `lib`/`include`
before invoking the installer and put them back when the install fails or does not
verify, which recovers `lib`/`include` without waiting for a script release;
`moon.exe` still has to be reinstalled on Windows.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `moon upgrade` on a working install.
2. Fail it after the download — Ctrl-C during `Downloading core ...` /
   `Bundling core ...`, or block `cli.moonbitlang.com/cores/`.
3. `moon check` now fails in every project; `lib` is empty.

## Environment

Operating System: Windows 11 (ordering is identical on Unix)

```
moon 0.1.20261119 (738607b 2026-11-19) ~\.moon\bin\moon.exe
moonc v0.10.22+124d61d05 (2026-11-19) ~\.moon\bin\moonc.exe
moonrun 0.1.20261119 (738607b 2026-11-19) ~\.moon\bin\moonrun.exe
```

Also reproduced on 0.1.20261117 and 0.1.20261104 (the latter predates #2594).

- [x] (Optional) My case is minimal enough to be reproducible.

title: moonrun: --test-args parse errors hide the format and which moonrun parsed it

labels.name: pending-triage
labels.description: This issue is not confirmed yet, and/or hasn't been checked for priority

body:
## Actual behavior

When moonrun cannot parse a `--test-args` value, the error gives neither the format
nor the binary that failed:

```
$ moonrun --test-args='x:"hello' hello.blackbox_test.wasm
Error: invalid MoonBit test arguments
Caused by:
    invalid test range "\"hello"
```

The expected format is already documented at `crates/moonrun/src/engine.rs:230`
(`filename:start-end,start-end/...`), but never reaches the user.

This is most confusing when `moon` and `moonrun` come from different builds. #2457
replaced the JSON selection payload with the compact format and explicitly assumes
the harness selects a moonrun built from the same sources as moon. A moon released
before #2457 still sends JSON; the compact decoder splits it by `/`, and because
package names are `owner/pkg`, the owner name is quoted back at the user:

```
$ moonrun --test-args='{"package":"hello/world","file_and_index":[["a.mbt",[{"start":0,"end":1}]]]}' hello.blackbox_test.wasm
Error: invalid MoonBit test arguments
Caused by:
    invalid test range "\"hello"
```

Nothing in that output points at a toolchain mismatch.

I am not asking to keep the old wire format or to roll back #2457 — the compact
format is an improvement. This is only about the error message.

## Expected Behavior

Add one context layer where `--test-args` is parsed (`RunOptions::parsed_test_args`,
`crates/moonrun/src/engine.rs:236`), carrying the version *and the resolved binary
path*:

```
Error: invalid MoonBit test arguments (moonrun 0.1.20261119 at ~\.moon\bin\moonrun.exe; expected format: filename:start-end,start-end/...)
Caused by:
    invalid test range "\"hello"
```

Both values already exist: `moonrun --version` prints the version, and
`std::env::current_exe()` gives the path. Without the path a user still has to run
`moon --version` separately to discover that a leftover moonrun from `PATH` was used.

Related observation (not part of this request): when `~/.moon/bin/moonrun` is absent,
`crates/moonutil/src/binaries.rs:93-107` silently falls back to `PATH`, which is what
allows the mismatch in the first place. `MOONRUN_OVERRIDE` already exists as an
explicit escape hatch; a warning on fallback would be a separate change.

Related: #2506, #2453 and #2425 are open refactors that already touch
`crates/moonrun/src/engine.rs`. None of them changes the `FromStr` impl that
produces these errors — mentioning them here in case this context layer
could ride along with that in-flight work.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use any compiled blackbox test wasm (e.g. the output of `moon test --build-only`).
2. Run `moonrun --test-args='x:"hello' <that wasm>`.
3. Observe the error above. Happens every time; parsing occurs before the runtime is
   created (`engine.rs:591`).

For the mismatch variant, call a post-#2457 `moonrun` with a JSON payload from a
pre-#2457 `moon`, or run the exact command in Actual behavior.

## Environment

Operating System: Windows 11 (parser is platform-independent)

```
moon 0.1.20261119 (738607b 2026-11-19)
moonrun 0.1.20261119 (738607b 2026-11-19)
```

## Checklist

- [x] (Optional) My case is minimal enough to be reproducible.

title: `moon upgrade` fails on Windows due to hardcoded PowerShell 5.1 invocation (ExtractToDirectory overload missing & Security module load error)

labels.name: pending-triage
labels.description: This issue is not confirmed yet, and/or hasn't been checked for priority

body:
## Problem Description
Running `moon upgrade` on Windows fails with two concurrent errors, even when PowerShell 7.x is installed and set as the default shell. The root cause is that `moon upgrade` internally invokes `powershell.exe` (Windows PowerShell 5.1) instead of `pwsh.exe`, leading to:
1. `Cannot find an overload for "ExtractToDirectory" and the argument count: "3"` — .NET Framework 4.x (used by PS 5.1) lacks the 3-parameter `ZipFile.ExtractToDirectory` overload available in .NET Core/.NET 5+.
2. `Set-ExecutionPolicy : module 'Microsoft.PowerShell.Security' could not be loaded` — PS 5.1 Security module fails to load in certain environments.

## Environment
- OS: Windows 11 (Build 26100)
- PowerShell 7 version: 7.7.0
- Windows PowerShell version: 5.1.26100.9818 (verified via `powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command '$PSVersionTable.PSVersion'`)
- Installed .NET Runtimes: Microsoft.NETCore.App 6.0.36, 7.0.20, 8.0.30, 9.0.19, 10.0.15
- MoonBit CLI version: 0.1.20261119

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open a PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`) terminal on Windows.
2. Run `moon upgrade`.
3. Observe the installation script execution failure.

## Expected Behavior
`moon upgrade` should either:
- Invoke `pwsh.exe` explicitly to leverage modern .NET runtime support, OR
- Use a PowerShell 5.1-compatible extraction method (e.g., 2-parameter `ExtractToDirectory` or `Expand-Archive`), OR
- Provide a documented workaround for Windows users.

## Actual Behavior
The command fails with:
```
Set-ExecutionPolicy : ... found in the module 'Microsoft.PowerShell.Security', but the module could not be loaded
At C:\Users\HP\AppData\Local\Temp.tmp9nkSgg\script.ps1:1 char:1
...
Cannot find an overload for "ExtractToDirectory" and the argument count: "3"
```
## Workaround Verified
Manually running the official install script **in pwsh 7** succeeds without errors:
```powershell
Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser
irm https://cli.moonbitlang.com/install/powershell.ps1 | iex
```
This confirms the issue is specific to `moon upgrade`'s internal shell invocation, not the system environment or script logic itself.
## Additional Context
- Microsoft has officially deprecated Windows PowerShell 5.1 as of November 2026; future Windows versions will no longer ship it by default.
- The 3-parameter `ExtractToDirectory(String, String, Boolean)` overload is documented as .NET Core/.NET 5+ only and does not exist in .NET Framework 4.x.
- Suggested fix: Update `moon upgrade` to detect and prefer `pwsh.exe`, or fall back to PS 5.1-compatible APIs.

title: [native] Discuss diagnostic policy for Clang C compilation
body:
Split from https://github.com/moonbitlang/moon/issues/2479, originally proposed by @wzzc-dev.

## Proposal to evaluate
The original report asks Moon to downgrade selected Clang C diagnostics for MSVC-classified stub compilation, including incompatible pointer types, implicit function declarations, integer conversions, and incompatible function-pointer types.

This issue records that request for discussion; it does not endorse globally disabling or downgrading these diagnostics.

## Why this needs a policy decision
Such diagnostics can reveal real ABI/type mismatches, invalid calls, or unsafe conversions. Blanket suppression could hide defects in user stubs, dependencies, or runtime code. Compiler/version-specific behavior and the distinction between a warning and a default error also matter.

The version claims in the source reports differ: #2479 attributes the incompatible-pointer-types default error to Clang >=16, while the linked runtime PR discusses Clang 22. Verify the relevant diagnostic and exact compiler mode/version before relying on either threshold.

## Relationship to the runtime fix
The concrete `GetExitCodeProcess(handle, out)` pointer mismatch is already tracked in https://github.com/moonbitlang/moonbit-native-runtime/pull/6 (open when this issue was extracted). Do not duplicate that source-fix issue or imply that a diagnostic-policy change resolves it. The original report also links https://github.com/moonbitlang/async/pull/721 for the corresponding async source.

## Discussion / validation
Compare fixing incompatible source types, retaining compiler defaults, targeted compatibility flags, and explicit user opt-in. Define affected compilation stages and compiler families before changing defaults; validate representative supported compiler versions and regression coverage.

The original reporter's `CL=-Wno-error=incompatible-pointer-types` workaround is reported context, not a general recommendation.

---

title: [native] Discuss an invocation-wide native compiler flags override
body:
Split from https://github.com/moonbitlang/moon/issues/2479, originally proposed by @wzzc-dev.

## Motivation
The original report requests a user CFLAGS override, for example an environment variable or moon.work configuration, to customize native compilation without changing individual dependency packages.

This is about invocation-wide/user-side control, not claiming that package-level compiler configuration is absent. Existing package configuration includes `stub-cc-flags` for C stub compilation; see https://github.com/moonbitlang/moon/blob/main/crates/moonbuild/template/pkg.schema.json.

## Decisions needed
- Interface: environment variable, CLI option, workspace configuration, or another mechanism.
- Scope: local package stubs, dependency stubs, generated native code, and/or shipped runtime compilation. These are separate choices, not an agreed blanket scope.
- Precedence and merge semantics relative to tool defaults and package-specific flags; whether the override appends, replaces, or selectively overrides them.
- Compiler-family handling, argument quoting, and build-cache invalidation/reproducibility.

## Original workaround and limitations
The reporter used `MOON_CC` to select clang-cl and its `CL` environment variable to pass `-Wno-error=incompatible-pointer-types`. That is compiler-specific behavior, not a portable Moon compiler-flags interface.

The separate runtime source fix is tracked by https://github.com/moonbitlang/moonbit-native-runtime/pull/6. An override should not be treated as a substitute for fixing a source defect.

---
AI-assisted extraction; this is a design request, not a claim of independent reproduction or an agreed flag precedence.

title: [native/windows] Avoid conflicting C and C++ language-standard flags for C++ stubs
body:
Split from https://github.com/moonbitlang/moon/issues/2479, originally reported by @wzzc-dev. This extracted report has not been independently reproduced.

## Reported behavior
The original report says Moon injects `/std:c11` into MSVC-classified stub compilation even for C++ stubs whose package supplies `/std:c++20`. It reports that `cl.exe` rejects the combination with D8016, motivating a switch to clang-cl.

Reported environment: moon 0.1.20261104 (940aa18), Windows 11 x64, MSVC 14.44 / VS 2022 Community, Windows SDK 10.0.26100. The original report also used clang-cl 23.1.0. It does not include a self-contained C++ stub fixture or the complete failing cl.exe command.

## Scope
Investigate how language mode and standard flags are selected for C versus C++ stubs. A C++ stub should not receive conflicting C-only standard flags. Possible approaches from the original report include C-only injection or respecting an explicitly selected C++ standard; the exact fix remains to be decided.

## Validation needed
Capture a minimal C++ stub package and generated command, reproduce the claimed D8016 with cl.exe, and test C-only, C++-only, and mixed stub packages. Preserve required C behavior while fixing C++ handling.

The separate shipped-runtime pointer mismatch is tracked by https://github.com/moonbitlang/moonbit-native-runtime/pull/6 and is not part of this issue.

title: [js backend] foreign_library artifact silently returns wrong results (same code correct in test/native builds)
body:
## Summary

The same source produces different results depending on the **build context**: a `foreign_library` package built for the `js` backend returns **wrong results silently**, while `moon test --target js` and the native build of the identical code are correct.

The wrong result is not an error — it is a JSON envelope reporting `ok:true` with a corrupted payload (length correct, contents wrong).

## Environment

- moon `0.1.20261104 (940aa18 2026-11-04)`
- moonc `v0.10.20+65efd5b93`
- Node `v24.14.0`
- Windows `10.0.26200`
- Repo: `https://github.com/vicTop-cw/QRFlux` @ `f520304`

## Reproduction

```sh
git clone https://github.com/vicTop-cw/QRFlux
cd QRFlux
moon build --target js
node scripts/repro_wasm_export_issue.cjs   # exits 1 when the issue reproduces
```

Output (deterministic):

```
expected payload hex : 4869            ("Hi")
native CLI (correct) : Hi
js artifact (foreign): 52565457        <-- wrong, no error signalled
```

The artifact under test is the `foreign_library` package `src/wasmapi` (see `src/wasmapi/moon.pkg`), which exports
`qrflux_decode_image_png(base64Png) -> String` via `#export_name`, and internally calls into
`src/web` → `src/qr`:

`base64 decode → PNG decode (zlib via core/compress/zlib) → Otsu binarize → finder localization → affine/perspective resample → QR payload`

## Where it diverges (step-by-step instrumentation)

| Step | Expected | Observed in the foreign_library js artifact |
|---|---|---|
| base64 → PNG bytes | PNG signature `0x89` | `first=137` — correct |
| PNG → grayscale | 290×290 | 290×290 — correct |
| grayscale → payload | `4869` | `52565457` — **wrong** |

## Individually verified correct *inside the same artifact*

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| traversal of a 14784-char string, in-package and cross-package | identical to the JS side |
| 11088 Buffer writes, byte-by-byte verified | `bad=0` |
| pure arithmetic via a cross-package call | correct |
| in-package base64 decode (the same logic, compiled *inside* the foreign_library package) | byte-exact (PNG signature OK) |
| same code under `moon test --target js` (1323 tests incl. PNG roundtrip and perspective) | all pass |
| same code, native (CLI `--decode-image-b64`) | correct |

Also ruled out: `--release` optimization (identical in a debug build), the standard library base64 decoder (a local re-implementation behaves the same), iterator vs. indexed access, and short cross-package calls.

## Suspected cause

A code-generation / build-context difference for the `js` backend when the consuming package is a `foreign_library`. The failing step is `decode_from_pixels` (or its transitive callees) inside `src/qr`; every input reaching it is proven correct.

## Notes

I could not reduce this to a smaller standalone case. The repo/commit above is the smallest reproduction I have, and the repro script is deterministic. Happy to run further instrumentation or share the generated `.js` artifact.

title: Feature request: a build-wide switch to leave `SourceLoc` autofill out (or pass custom `-cfg` from moon)
body:
## What we do

Our UI framework (mbui) records where each UI node and each of its properties was made, using `#callsite(autofill(loc))` + `loc~ : SourceLoc` on its node-making and property-setting functions (~260 of them). Tests read these places, so a failing check can name the line that made the widget.

Release builds only pass the place along and keep none of it, but every call site still gets its `SourceLoc` string compiled in: our app's release Wasm grows from 41.87 MB to 42.80 MB (+929 KB, +2.2%). The per-frame instruction cost is effectively zero; the size is the only cost.

## What we'd like

Either one of these would let us drop the cost in release builds and keep a single API:

1. **A build-wide setting that makes `SourceLoc` autofill produce an empty/shared constant** (e.g. `moon build --no-source-loc`, or a `moon.mod` / main package option), so call sites compile no per-site string. The parameter stays, the signatures stay the same.
2. **Custom `#cfg` flags passed from `moon`** (`moon build --cfg sources=off`, `moon test --cfg …`), as asked in #972 and #1785. `moonc` already takes `-cfg flag=value`, but `moon` has no way to pass it through.

(1) fits this case better: with (2) we would still have to write two signatures for every function, since the call sites forward `loc~` and that only type-checks in one of them.

## Environment

```
moon 0.1.20261016 (1af328f 2026-10-16)
```
Debug vs release does not help us here: our tests run with `--release` too, and they are the ones that need the places.

title: [native/windows] bare `MOON_CC=clang-cl` runs the discovered `cl.exe`; only a full path selects clang-cl

labels.name: pending-triage
labels.description: This issue is not confirmed yet, and/or hasn't been checked for priority

body:
Environment: moon 0.1.20261104 (940aa18), Windows 11 26200, clang-cl 22.1.4 (MSVC-target install), MSVC 14.51.

## Repro

```text
moon new probe && cd probe          # each build preceded by `moon clean`
MOON_CC=clang-cl     moon build --target native
MOON_CC=clang-cl.exe moon build --target native
MOON_CC=C:\clang+llvm-22.1.4-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc\bin\clang-cl.exe moon build --target native
llvm-strings _build/native/debug/build/runtime-process.obj | grep -E "clang version|Microsoft \(R\)"
# add --release and read _build/native/release/build/runtime-process.obj
```

The object file is the only observable: `-v` prints no toolchain line and stderr stays silent on success.

## Behavior

| `MOON_CC` | warning | record in `.obj` | profile |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clang-cl` / `clang-cl.exe` (bare) | none | `Microsoft (R) Optimizing Compiler` | debug **and** `--release` |
| full path to `clang-cl.exe` | none (clang's own warnings still print) | `clang version 22.1.4 ...` | debug **and** `--release` |

The toolchain does distinguish *incompatible* drivers: `MOON_CC=clang` in debug prints `MOON_CC is ignored ... set MOON_CC to cl.exe or clang-cl.exe ...` and falls back to MSVC, and `--release` honors clang. It does not distinguish a bare cl-compatible driver that names a different compiler.

## Root cause — both backends converge on `resolve_msvc_toolchain_override`

- debug / new native backend: `windows_msvc_native_toolchain()` (msvc.rs)
- release / generated-C: `resolve_native_toolchain_executables()` (compiler_flags.rs)

Both test `is_path_like_tool` (`is_absolute() || has_parent`, so bare names never qualify) and land in the same override with this comment:

```text
// A bare override selects the discovered toolchain as a whole. Path-like overrides
// remain self-contained so they cannot inherit an environment for another installation.

toolchain.cc.cc_path.clone_from(&resolved.cc.cc_path);  // discovered cl.exe
toolchain.cc.ar_path.clone_from(&resolved.cc.ar_path);  // discovered lib.exe
```

## Why it matters

- The dev reference documents the rule with `cl.exe` as its example, where the substitution is an identity transform — so the clang-cl consequence was never visible.
- Besides the compiler, the librarian swaps (`llvm-lib.exe` → `lib.exe`) and clang-only diagnostics on the shipped runtime vanish (`process.c(221) -Wparentheses`, `io_windows.c(355,411) -Wswitch`).
- Nothing discloses it: the manual says 可执行文件名称**或路径**； the warning recommends `cl.exe or clang-cl.exe`; stderr stays silent; `-v` prints no toolchain line; `--release` never warns about the toolchain at all.
- `clang-cl` is the only clang-family cl-compatible driver, so the swap defeats the intent users pick it for (dodging #2254's cl /O2 cliff).
- No test pins it: the bare-name tests cover only `cl.exe` (`bare_windows_msvc_resolution_uses_discovery`, `bare_windows_msvc_package_override_uses_discovered_tool_paths`) — the identity case.

This is a false green: no warning, a successful build, and the compiler record inside the `.obj` is the only tell.

## Ask

1. If a bare override's basename differs from the discovered driver's, error out or emit the existing `MOON_CC is ignored ...` warning; keep bare `cl.exe` exactly as today.
2. Or fix the disclosure: the warning text and the manual should say a bare name selects the discovered toolchain and that `clang-cl` needs a full path, and the dev reference's example should be a non-identity one instead of `cl.exe`.

Workaround today: spell `MOON_CC` as a full path on Windows.
Found while re-verifying #2254 / #2479.

title: [native/windows] shipped runtime process.c + /std:c11 injection break clang-cl >= 16 builds
body:
## Environment

- moon: 0.1.20261104 (940aa18 2026-11-04)
- OS: Windows 11 x64, MSVC 14.44 (VS 2022 Community), Windows SDK 10.0.26100
- C compiler: clang-cl 23.1.0 (MSVC-compatible mode; required, see "Context" below)

## Reproduction

Any MoonBit project with native C stubs on Windows:

```sh
set MOON_CC=C:\path\to\clang-cl.exe
moon build --target native
```

Two independent failure modes appear.

### 1. Shipped runtime: LPDWORD mismatch is a hard error under clang >= 16

`%USERPROFILE%\.moon\lib\runtime\process.c`, line 58 (shipped with the toolchain):

```c
int moonbit_rt_get_process_result(HANDLE handle, int32_t pid, int32_t *out) {
  ...
  BOOL ret = GetExitCodeProcess(handle, out);   // out is int32_t*, parameter is LPDWORD
```

clang >= 16 promotes `-Wincompatible-pointer-types` from a warning to a `DefaultError` diagnostic (cl.exe only warns, which is why MSVC-only CI does not catch it):

```text
C:\Users\...\moon\lib\runtime\process.c(58,41): error: incompatible pointer types passing 'int32_t *' (aka 'int *') to parameter of type 'LPDWORD' (aka 'unsigned long *') [-Wincompatible-pointer-types]
1 error generated.
Error: failed to run build for target Native
```

Request: change it to `GetExitCodeProcess(handle, (LPDWORD)out);` in the next toolchain release. The runtime sources are not in an open repository, so I cannot send a PR for this file directly; `DWORD` and `int32_t` are both 4 bytes on Windows, so the cast is behavior-neutral.

### 2. Same pattern upstream in moonbitlang/async

`moonbitlang/async/src/internal/event_loop/process.c` line 50 has the identical call. Filed a PR with the same one-line fix: https://github.com/moonbitlang/async/pull/721

### Context: why clang-cl is required on Windows at all

The CLI unconditionally injects `/std:c11` for every MSVC-classified stub compile, while packages with C++ stubs (e.g. Skia bindings) emit `/std:c++20`. `cl.exe` rejects that pair with D8016, so Windows native builds are effectively forced onto clang-cl, where newer clang's stricter C diagnostics then surface (see item 1).

If `/std:c11` were injected only for C stubs (or skipped when stub flags already carry `/std:c++`), plain `cl.exe` would work again and the clang-cl exposure would disappear. Not sure whether the unconditional injection is intentional (for wgpu_mbt's `<stdatomic.h>`?), so filing this as a question + proposals:

1. Fix the runtime cast (item 1).
2. Inject `-Wno-error=incompatible-pointer-types` (and the other clang-16 `DefaultError` C diagnostics: `-Wimplicit-function-declaration`, `-Wint-conversion`, `-Wincompatible-function-pointer-types`) for MSVC-classified stub compiles.
3. Make `/std:c11` injection conditional (C-only, or skip when stub flags carry `/std:c++*`).
4. Expose a user CFLAGS override (env var or moon.work config).

Current user-side workaround: `CL=-Wno-error=incompatible-pointer-types` env var (clang-cl reads `CL`) + `MOON_CC=<clang-cl path>`.

title: refactor(registry): follow up on temporary directories and reclone recovery
body:
The Git index and symbols synchronization split preserves pre-existing filesystem and recovery behavior. Track the following cleanups separately from the release-cache and synchronization separation.

- [ ] Replace `unique_sibling_dir` with the existing `tempfile` dependency. Create staging directories on the destination filesystem and make ownership of the new checkout, extracted symbols, and backups explicit. Preserve the original data when publication or rollback fails; automatic cleanup must not remove the only surviving backup.
- [ ] Clarify Git reclone decisions and preserve the underlying update error. `RemoteMismatch` is a configuration decision, `NotGitRepository` and `MissingOrigin` describe unusable cache state, and `UpdateFailed` describes an operation failure. Avoid reducing `fetch_and_reset_registry_index` to `.is_ok()` or treating every fetch/reset failure as a reason to reclone. Keep recovery and its diagnostics inside Git synchronization, and distinguish failures that rebuilding can repair from network, authentication, and access failures.

The `generation` marker is also pre-existing: it was introduced in 6a98f5e43 (`perf: optimize registry updates`). It records a successful synchronization so a caller that waited for the lock can reuse overlapping work. It is neither a Git commit identifier nor a TTL, and can change even when HEAD does not. Any later naming or bookkeeping cleanup should preserve that behavior and keep symbols ETag validation distinct.

Retain coverage for failed clone/publication/rollback, preservation of the previous checkout, same-source concurrent update reuse, and independent symbols refreshes.

title: test(moonrun): audit executable fixtures against concurrent fork inheritance
body:
## Problem

Linux executable-fixture tests can observe `ETXTBSY` (26) instead of the expected `ENOEXEC` (8) when another parallel test forks while the fixture is open for writing. Closing the writer in the creating process does not close an inherited writer in the fork child; CLOEXEC takes effect only on successful exec. This can invalidate a test's assumptions without changing the spawn implementation.

In #2429, `process::ambient::tests::executable_text_keeps_the_platform_search_fallback` failed at `ambient.rs:1397` on head `01e773770fc6d99cb9d302eb514b395408518f05`: [failed job](https://github.com/moonbitlang/moon/actions/runs/41568584633/job/125695976668). The same head passed after one retry, with no code or test changes: [successful retry](https://github.com/moonbitlang/moon/actions/runs/41568584633/job/125708196717). This PR did not modify that test or the native spawn implementation.

A controlled native `posix_spawn` reproduction returns 26 while a fork child retains the fixture writer and 8 after that child is reaped, with identical file contents and arguments. The CI log does not identify the process that retained a writer, so the exact CI interleaving remains unconfirmed. A related test in `ambient/fork_exec.rs` was previously isolated in #2413.

## Follow-up

Audit this class of tests together rather than adding another per-test self-exec wrapper immediately:

- Inventory tests that create executable fixtures while other tests fork or spawn, including raw-fork tests and the explicit fork/exec fallback.
- Establish a reproducible concurrency scenario and examine fixture publication, writer lifetime and test-runner isolation across Linux and macOS.
- Compare pre-created immutable fixtures, a dedicated integration-test executable with deliberate scheduling, and a shared fixture/isolation strategy. A fixture-local mutex alone does not serialize unrelated forks.
- Preserve strict platform-specific spawn/error assertions and direct-versus-PATH behavior. Do not accept ETXTBSY as equivalent to ENOEXEC, add sleeps or retry loops to hide it, or alter native production behavior merely to stabilize tests.
- Document the chosen harness invariant and apply it consistently to the affected tests; reconsider existing one-off isolation where appropriate.

For now, retain the existing implementation and tests. This issue records the broader audit separately from policy configuration and IPC development.

title: moon bench --target wasm --release does not run wasm-opt
body:
When evaluating a Wasm performance change, I expected `moon bench --target wasm --release` to include a `wasm-opt` post-link optimization pass. The current benchmark build plan does not include one, even when `wasm-opt` is available on PATH.

Reproduction using moonbitlang/core PR https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/pull/4585 (head `cac193930b7d04b02908b070a4e36f9de989adc3`):

```sh
moon bench builtin/clamped_view_bench_test.mbt --target wasm --release --no-parallelize --dry-run
moon bench builtin/clamped_view_bench_test.mbt --target wasm --release --no-parallelize
```

The dry-run plan contains 3 `moon generate-test-driver` commands, 65 `moonc build-package` commands, and 3 `moonc link-core` commands. There is no `wasm-opt` command. The Wasm benchmark is subsequently executed with `moonrun`; it is not automatically passed through Binaryen's optimizer. This describes the missing post-link pass, not an absence of MoonBit compiler optimizations or runtime JIT optimization.

Toolchain:

```text
moon 0.1.20261029 (ee2274c 2026-10-29)
moonc v0.10.19+74b7643b8 (2026-10-29)
moonrun 0.1.20261029 (ee2274c 2026-10-29)
wasm-opt version 121 (version_121), available on PATH
```

For performance comparisons intended to represent a deployment pipeline that uses `wasm-opt`, both baseline and candidate need the same post-link optimization pass. Otherwise source-level changes to function splitting or branching may look beneficial before optimization without establishing the same benefit after optimization. This matters when comparing against optimized native builds as well.

Could release-mode Wasm benchmarks run `wasm-opt`, or expose an explicit supported option for doing so? The verbose output should make the optimizer version/options and executed artifact clear, and documentation should state whether release benchmarks include this step. The invocation also needs feature flags appropriate to the emitted module (e.g. SIMD and multivalue); plain `wasm-opt -O3` without feature flags rejects this benchmark module.

title: Windows: moon test --target js/wasm-gc fails with os error 206 (driver gets the whole file_and_index JSON as one argument)
body:
On Windows, `moon test --target js` (and `--target wasm-gc`) fails for a package with many files: the test driver is spawned with the whole `{"package":...,"file_and_index":[...]}` JSON as one command-line argument, and once that passes Windows' 32,767-character command-line limit, `CreateProcess` refuses it with os error 206. `--target native` passes the same package.

### Reproduce (bash, Windows)

```sh
mkdir manyfiles && cd manyfiles
printf 'name = "repro/manyfiles"\nversion = "0.1.0"\n' > moon.mod
: > moon.pkg
printf '///|\npub fn one() -> Int {\n  1\n}\n' > lib.mbt
for i in $(seq -w 1 200); do
  printf '///|\ntest "case %s" {\n  assert_eq(@manyfiles.one(), 1)\n}\n' $i \
    > "a_fairly_long_descriptive_test_file_name_number_${i}_test.mbt"
done
moon test --target js
```

```
Error: failed to run test for target Js
Caused by:
    0: Failed to run test for repro/manyfiles BlackboxTest
    1: Failed to spawn command Command { std: "...\node.exe" "--enable-source-maps" "...\_build\js\debug\test\manyfiles.blackbox_test.js" "{\"package\":\"repro/manyfiles\",\"file_and_index\":[[\"lib.mbt\",[]],[...
    2: The filename or extension is too long. (os error 206)
```

| test files | js | wasm-gc | native |
|---|---|---|---|
| 100 | pass | | |
| 200 | os error 206 | os error 206 | pass (200/200) |

We hit it in a real package (UsaGui's root package, a few hundred files). Passing the test list through a file or stdin (or only the files that hold tests) would avoid the limit.

### Environment

- moon 0.1.20261028 (e1e1f15), moonc v0.10.18+6c83a7f62 (2026-10-28); moon 0.1.20261012 / moonc v0.10.15 fails the same way

title: `moon prove` prints a stale "Succeeded" summary when a package fails before Why3 runs
body:
`moon prove` prints a stale "Succeeded" summary when a package fails before Why3 runs

When a package hits a type error or a proof-lowering error, `moon prove` prints the diagnostics and then the per-package result and summary from the *previous* run's `_build/verif/**/<pkg>.proof.json`. A package that doesn't compile is reported as `Succeeded` and counted in "N of N packages proved". The exit status is correct (1).

## Actual behavior

After a successful run, I added a type error to `lib/lib.mbtp` and ran `moon prove` again:

```
Error: [4014]
   ╭─[ /private/tmp/prove-repro/lib/lib.mbt:3:24 ]
   │
 3 │   proof_require: small(x),
   │                        ┬
   │                        ╰── Expr Type Mismatch
        has type : Int64
        wanted   : Int
───╯
Error: [4014]
   ╭─[ /private/tmp/prove-repro/lib/lib.mbtp:3:7 ]
   │
 3 │   x < 100L
   │       ──┬─
   │         ╰─── Expr Type Mismatch
        has type : Int64
        wanted   : Int
───╯
repro/prove_stale/lib
  Succeeded: 1 goals proved

Summary:
  1 of 1 packages proved
  1 goals proved
```

Exit status: 1. The mtime of `_build/verif/repro/prove_stale/lib/lib.proof.json` doesn't change, so Why3 doesn't run and the summary is read back from the old report.

It happens for every error that stops the run before Why3, with a warm cache:

| Change after a successful run | Error | Stale `Succeeded`? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Type error in a `.mbtp` predicate | 4014 | yes |
| Type error in a contract in the `.mbt` (`result > "x"`) | 4014 | yes |
| Type error in an uncontracted function in the same package | 4014 | yes |
| Code that passes `moon check` but that proof lowering rejects (`let _ = [1]` in a contracted body) | 4207 | yes |
| Same, inside a workspace member (`moon -C a prove`; report at `<workspace>/_build/verif/repro/a/lib/lib.proof.json`) | 4014 | yes |

A real proof failure (a goal that times out) does rewrite the report and prints `Failed` correctly, so only errors before Why3 are affected.

The last row of the table is the most misleading case: `moon check` is clean and the summary says everything is proved.

A related problem occurs with a cold cache. In a module with packages `lib` (broken) and `lib2` (fine), after `rm -rf _build/verif`:

```
Error: [4014]
Error: [4014]
repro/prove_stale/lib2
  Succeeded: 1 goals proved

Summary:
  1 of 1 packages proved
  1 goals proved
```

`lib` is missing from the count entirely; the summary should say 1 of 2. With a warm cache the same layout prints `2 of 2 packages proved`.

## Expected Behavior

A package that fails to typecheck or to lower should be reported as failed (or not attempted) and counted in the total, e.g.:

```
repro/prove_stale/lib
  Failed: did not compile

Summary:
  0 of 1 packages proved
```

Its previous `proof.json` shouldn't be presented as the current result. Deleting or invalidating the report before lowering would also stop later steps or tools from reading it.

## Steps to Reproduce


`moon.mod`:

```
name = "repro/prove_stale"

version = "0.1.0"
```

`lib/moon.pkg`:

```
proof_enabled = true
```

`lib/lib.mbt`:

```moonbit
///|
pub fn inc(x : Int64) -> Int64 where {
  proof_require: small(x),
  proof_ensure: result => result > x,
} {
  x + 1L
}
```

`lib/lib.mbtp`:

```moonbit
///|
predicate small(x : Int64) {
  x < 100L
}
```

1. `moon prove`: prints `Succeeded: 1 goals proved` and exits 0.
2. In `lib/lib.mbtp`, change `small(x : Int64)` to `small(x : Int)`.
3. `moon prove`: prints the two type errors, then `Succeeded: 1 goals proved` / `1 of 1 packages proved`, and exits 1.
4. `rm -rf _build/verif && moon prove`: prints the same errors and no summary, and exits 1.

For the cold-cache miscount, copy `lib` to `lib2` before step 1, then do steps 2 and 4.

## Environment

Operating System: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64)

```
moon 0.1.20261020 (2284bd2 2026-10-20) ~/.moon/bin/moon
moonc v0.10.16+b1a0e846e (2026-10-16) ~/.moon/bin/moonc
moonrun 0.1.20261020 (2284bd2 2026-10-20) ~/.moon/bin/moonrun

Feature flags enabled: rr_moon_mod,rr_moon_pkg
```

## Checklist

- [x] (Optional) My case is minimal enough to be reproducible.

title: Define exact-version registry queries and metadata refresh semantics
body:
## Motivation

Moon’s MVS traverses metadata at declared versions, then selects versions required by the graph. Every declared version must exist; substituting an available release would make resolution depend on registry changes. #2360 establishes this invariant, so resolution only needs exact-version metadata.

With on-demand queries in #2351, we also need a freshness contract. Dependencies and checksums are immutable, while latest-version answers and deprecation status can change.

## Metadata and caching

Support two queries:

- **Exact version:** return the requested release’s identity, dependencies, checksum, and current deprecation status.
- **Latest:** return the latest release for the requested module, following existing selection rules.

Persist exact records by registry, module, and version, including records traversed but ultimately unselected by MVS. Persist latest answers separately; arbitrary cached releases do not constitute a complete version list.

Refreshing deprecation status must not silently replace dependencies or checksums. Conflicting immutable metadata should produce an error and preserve the valid cache.

## Command behavior

Keep existing Git-index behavior when the environment switch is disabled. With `MOON_REGISTRY_API=1`, use the following contract:

| Operation | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `check/build/test` | Reuse exact metadata; fetch missing records; report locally known deprecation warnings |
| Frozen resolution | Use cached metadata; fail on missing records |
| Unversioned `add/fetch` | Query latest online and use the returned concrete version |
| Exact `add/fetch` | Reuse immutable content and refresh the requested version’s deprecation status |
| `add/fetch --no-update` | Reuse cached mutable information; allow acquisition of missing exact content |
| `moon update` | Refresh the current project’s dependency status and report available updates |

Preserve the distinction between executable selectors that prefer cached latest and explicit `@latest` requests.

Ordinary builds should not refresh metadata because of its age. No TTL is needed initially. Deprecation remains advisory and covers final selected direct and transitive registry dependencies.

## API-mode `moon update`

The command should:

1. Resolve the current dependency graph.
2. Refresh status for every selected registry version.
3. Query latest for those module identities and report available updates.
4. Persist the results for subsequent builds.

Refreshing latest alone is insufficient: a healthy `1.1.0` says nothing about whether the project’s cached `1.0.0` was recently deprecated.

This operation does not modify dependency declarations, install sources, or execute package hooks. Workspace scope follows existing resolution rules; execution outside a project reports an error.

Explicit refresh must query or revalidate online. Reading a cached answer must not count as a refresh.

## Failure behavior

- Required latest queries must not silently fall back to stale answers.
- An unversioned `--no-update` request without a cached latest answer fails clearly.
- An exact operation with valid content may continue with a warning if only its advisory refresh fails.
- `moon update` exits nonzero when refreshes fail and identifies incomplete results. Successful cache writes may remain.
- Finding updates or deprecated versions alone does not fail the command.

## Acceptance criteria

- Publishing unrelated releases does not change an existing dependency graph.
- A fully cached build makes no registry metadata requests, including across processes.
- After deprecation or restoration, `moon update` changes subsequent warnings without changing selected versions.
- Old selected versions are refreshed even when latest points elsewhere.
- Cached reads cannot suppress explicit refreshes.
- Frozen behavior, `--no-update`, and existing Git-index behavior remain covered by regression tests.

Related: #2351, #2360.

title: `moon deprecate` fails with HTTP 422 "Invalid module path" for a published module
body:
## Summary

`moon deprecate` fails for my published module `t-ujiie-g/moon-pptx`: the registry responds with `422 Unprocessable Entity: Invalid module path`. `--dry-run` on the same command lists all 17 published versions, so the module name itself resolves.

## Steps to reproduce

```console
$ moon whoami
Logged in as t-ujiie-g

$ moon deprecate --dry-run t-ujiie-g/moon-pptx --reason "x"
Would deprecate t-ujiie-g/moon-pptx@0.10.1: x
Would deprecate t-ujiie-g/moon-pptx@0.10.0: x
...  (all 17 versions listed)

$ moon deprecate t-ujiie-g/moon-pptx --reason "Moved to moonbitlang/pptx. Please migrate: moon add moonbitlang/pptx"
registry returned HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity: Invalid module path
Error: `moon deprecate` failed
```

The result is the same with or without a URL in `--reason`, so the reason text is not the cause. `-v` / `--trace` print nothing more.

## Expected

All published versions of `t-ujiie-g/moon-pptx` get marked deprecated with the given reason.

## Guess

Both the username (`t-ujiie-g`) and the module name (`moon-pptx`) contain hyphens. The read-only lookup that `--dry-run` uses accepts the path, but the write endpoint may validate module paths with a stricter pattern. I have not confirmed this.

## Context

This module was imported into `moonbitlang/office.mbt` as `moonbitlang/pptx`. I want to deprecate the old one so that existing users see the migration pointer. Related: #263.

## Environment

- moon 0.1.20261023 (3778465 2026-10-23)
- macOS (Darwin 25.6.0)

title: Native: enable /bigobj for MSVC builds to avoid object-file section limits
body:
## Motivation

Complex MoonBit projects built with `--target native` on Windows using MSVC may fail when a generated C translation unit produces an object file with too many sections.

According to [Microsoft's `/bigobj` documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/build/reference/bigobj-increase-number-of-sections-in-dot-obj-file?view=msvc-170), the default object-file limit is 65,279 addressable sections. Machine-generated code can exceed this limit and encounter compiler error C1128. `/bigobj` raises the section capacity to 2^32.

The relevant limit is the section count in a single object file, rather than overall project size. Large generated C files make this worth handling by default.

## Detailed Description

Please add `/bigobj` by default when Moon invokes MSVC to compile C sources for native builds, particularly the C emitted by `moonc link-core`.

This should be a compiler option, placed before any `/link` separator, and should apply only to compiler drivers that support it. Users should not need to add it manually for each affected project.

The current MSVC-specific compiler flags in `crates/moonutil/src/compiler_flags/msvc.rs` (`add_cc_specific_flags`) do not include `/bigobj`.

This is a preventive build robustness request. No minimal reproducer, Windows build log, or specific Moon/MSVC version is attached; it does not establish that a particular project's failure was caused by this limit.

## Related Issues

No existing issue was found by searching for `bigobj` or `C1128`.

## Checklist

- [x] I have added all necessary details to make it easy for the maintainers to understand my request.

title: bug(moonrun): Run teardown can hang when worker cancellation precedes a blocking syscall
Windows: dev_build inputs with `..` fail to stat after #2337 (verbatim package root)
body:
Since moon `0.1.20261020 (cf4a17e)`, a `dev_build` / `pre-build` input that leaves the package directory with `..` can't be stat'ed on Windows:

```
Error: failed to run build for target Native
Caused by:
    0: Failed to run n2 graph
    1: stat "\\?\D:\a\openseek\openseek\agent_tool\mbtx\..\..\share\workflow\change-review.mbtx": The filename, directory name, or volume label syntax is incorrect. (os error 123)
```

Reproducer: in a local module, a package `a/b/moon.pkg` with

```
dev_build(rule: "gen", input: ["../../share/x.txt"], output: "generated.mbt")
```

then `moon build --target native` on Windows. It works with moon `0.1.20261016 (1af328f)` and on macOS/Linux.

**Cause.** #2337 ("preserve canonical roots") keeps package roots in verbatim `\\?\` form. `resolve_custom_prebuild` (`crates/moonbuild-rupes-recta/src/build_plan/builders.rs`) still builds input and output paths with

```rust
RelativePath::new(path).normalize().to_path(&pkg.root_path)
```

`relative_path::RelativePath::normalize` keeps leading `..` because it can't resolve them without a base. `to_path` appends them to the verbatim root, and Win32 does no `..` processing on `\\?\` paths, so the stat fails.

**Suggested fix.** Resolve the components lexically against the root rather than appending them, for example:

```rust
let mut resolved = pkg.root_path.clone();
for component in RelativePath::new(path).normalize().components() {
    match component {
        relative_path::Component::Normal(name) => resolved.push(name),
        relative_path::Component::ParentDir => { resolved.pop(); }
        relative_path::Component::CurDir => {}
    }
}
```

This affects outputs too, and any other place that joins a user-supplied relative path onto a canonical root.

**Context.** The archive at `cli.moonbitlang.com/binaries/0.10.16%2Bb1a0e846e/` was re-uploaded on 2026-10-20 08:30 UTC with this moon build. That broke the Windows desktop packaging job in moonbitlang/openseek even though its toolchain pin hadn't changed. The workaround there is moonbitlang/openseek#2136.

title: moon upgrade always reinstalls even when toolchain is up to date
body:
`moon upgrade` never reports "Your toolchain is up to date"; it always falls
through to a full download and reinstall, even when `moon`, `moonc`, and
`moonrun` are already at the latest published versions.

## Environment

- `moon 0.1.20261016 (1af328f 2026-10-16)`, Linux x86_64
- `cli.moonbitlang.com/version.json` currently lists the same `0.1.20261016` /
  `v0.10.16` versions.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install a toolchain that is already the latest published version.
2. Run `moon upgrade` (without `--force` / `--dev`).
3. Expected: it prints "Your toolchain is up to date. You can use
   `moon upgrade --force` to force upgrade." and exits 0.
4. Actual: it proceeds to download and reinstall the toolchain.

## Root cause

`should_upgrade` in `crates/moonbuild/src/upgrade.rs` parses an 8-digit date out
of each tool's version string with `extract_date`, which only looks at the third
dot-separated component:

```rust
fn extract_date(input: &str) -> Option<String> {
    // from the second dot
    input.split('.').nth(2).and_then(|s| {
        let start = s.find(|c: char| c.is_ascii_digit())?;
        let date = s[start..].chars().take(8).collect::<String>();
        if date.len() == 8 && date.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) {
            Some(date)
        } else {
            None
        }
    })
}
```

This works for `moon` (`0.1.20261016 (1af328f 2026-10-16)`) and `moonrun`
(`moonrun 0.1.20261016 (1af328f 2026-10-16)`), but the `moonc` version is
`v0.10.16+b1a0e846e (2026-10-16)`. Splitting on `.` yields
`16+b1a0e846e (2026-10-16)` for the third component, whose first 8 characters are
`16+b1a0e` — not all digits — so `extract_date` returns `None`.

`should_upgrade` then propagates that `None`:

```rust
let moonc_version = get_moonc_version().ok()?;
let moonc_date = extract_date(&moonc_version)?;
```

and the caller only short-circuits on `Some(false)`:

```rust
if let Ok(data) = reqwest::blocking::get(version_url)
    && let Ok(latest_version_info) = data.json::<VersionItems>()
    && let Some(false) = should_upgrade(&latest_version_info)
{
    println!("Your toolchain is up to date. You can use `moon upgrade --force` to force upgrade.");
    return Ok(0);
}
```

`None` means "unknown", so the command always falls through to the reinstall
path.

## Impact

- The up-to-date fast path is effectively dead on current releases: `moon upgrade`
  always reinstalls.
- The same `None` fall-through also silently swallows network and JSON errors
  instead of surfacing them.

## Possible fix

Parse the date from the trailing `(YYYY-MM-DD)` group, or fall back to it when
the third component is not a bare date. Also distinguish "cannot determine"
from "up to date" so an unknown result can report an error rather than silently
reinstalling.

title: Publish self-contained native toolchain archives as GitHub release assets
body:
Publish self-contained native toolchain archives as GitHub release assets, so version managers such as mise, aqua and asdf can install MoonBit.

## Motivation

MoonBit cannot be installed with [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) today. The usual mise backends cannot find the binaries:

- `moonbitlang/moon` and `moonbitlang/core` have no GitHub releases.
- `moonbitlang/moonbit-compiler` has releases, but its only asset is `moonbit-wasm.tar.gz` (the WASM build of the compiler), not native binaries.
- The toolchain is only on the MoonBit CDN (`https://cli.moonbitlang.com/binaries/<version>/moonbit-<target>.tar.gz`), and the install script is the only supported way to install it.

Version managers make it easy to pin a toolchain version for each project and in CI. With GitHub release assets, `mise use github:moonbitlang/moon@<version>` could work without any MoonBit-specific code in mise. An entry in the aqua or mise registry would then be a small change.

## Detailed Description

For each release, attach native archives to a GitHub release, for example on `moonbitlang/moon`:

- `moonbit-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`
- `moonbit-linux-aarch64.tar.gz`
- `moonbit-darwin-aarch64.tar.gz`
- the Windows equivalent
- checksums (`.sha256`) for each archive

Each archive should be self-contained: extracting it gives a working toolchain. Today `install/unix.sh` does two more steps after it extracts the binaries:

1. It downloads `cores/core-<version>.tar.gz` separately into `lib/core`.
2. It runs `moon -C lib/core bundle --warn-list -a --target wasm-gc` to prebuild the standard library.

Generic installers cannot do these steps. If the release archive includes `lib/core`, already bundled for the default targets, extracting the archive is enough.

Release tags that are valid semver (like `v0.10.16+b1a0e846e`, which `moonbitlang/moonbit-compiler` already uses) also help version managers sort and resolve versions.

## Related Issues

- mise discussion: https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14713
- Community plugins that wrap the CDN today: [cometkim/asdf-moonbit](https://github.com/cometkim/asdf-moonbit), [maya0513/vfox-moonbit](https://github.com/maya0513/vfox-moonbit), [morning-start/vfox-moonbit](https://github.com/morning-start/vfox-moonbit)

## Checklist

- [x] I have added all necessary details to make it easy for the maintainers to understand my request.

title: Add a `--no-user-scripts` option for hosted builds

labels.name: pending-triage
labels.description: This issue is not confirmed yet, and/or hasn't been checked for priority

body:
Following [#2141](https://github.com/moonbitlang/moon/issues/2141), [#2160](https://github.com/moonbitlang/moon/pull/2160), and [#2162](https://github.com/moonbitlang/moon/pull/2162), Moon still lacks a reliable way to disable all package-controlled script execution.

Even with `MOON_IGNORE_PREBUILD=1` and `MOON_IGNORE_POSTADD=1`, this path remains possible:

```text
moon check / moon build --target wasm
  → install bin-deps
  → native/LLVM child build
  → execute --moonbit-unstable-prebuild
```

The child build selects its own backend, and module-level scripts ignore `MOON_IGNORE_PREBUILD`. This leaves hosted services processing untrusted packages, such as Mooncakes.io, exposed to arbitrary script execution during seemingly restricted builds.

Please provide a documented option such as `--no-user-scripts` that:

- Covers `pre-build` / `dev_build`, `--moonbit-unstable-prebuild`, and `postadd`.
- Propagates through dependency installation and all child builds, including dry runs.
- Rejects operations that cannot honor the policy, without silently falling back to script execution.

Other package-controlled execution paths, such as custom native compiler commands, should also be covered or explicitly rejected.

Hosted services need an enforceable no-user-script guarantee independent of the selected backend.

@peter-jerry-ye
